context.guidance: Require authentication on every route that returns Personal Data, and check on each request that the authenticated Data Principal owns the record or holds a role authorised for it. Do not let an identifier supplied in the path or body decide ownership. Apply the check to every method on the route, because Rule 6(1)(b) requires access to the resources holding Personal Data to be controlled.

value.fix: Stop trusting the raw path id and make the route authenticated and ownership-scoped. (1) Put an authentication middleware on this route, and on every other method that serves the same resource, so unauthenticated requests get a 401 before the handler runs. (2) Replace `JSON.parse(req.params.id)` with strict validation: accept only the expected type (e.g. a positive integer or UUID matched by a regex or a validator such as Joi/zod), and return 400 otherwise. Parsing arbitrary JSON lets callers pass objects or arrays into `where`, which can change query semantics. (3) Scope the query to the authenticated principal, for example `RecycleModel.findOne({ where: { id: recordId, ownerId: req.user.id } })`, or check `record.ownerId === req.user.id` (or a role that is authorised for the record) after loading it. Return 404 when no record matches so existence is not leaked. Do not take the owner or user identifier from `req.params` or `req.body`. (4) Apply the same check to GET, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE on this route, not only the method shown. (5) Add tests that confirm an unauthenticated request gets 401, a request for another user's record gets 404 or 403, a non-integer or object-shaped id gets 400, and the owner gets 200.
